title: The Immersive Edge: October 2026 industry content wrap-up
summary: The Immersive Edge, October 2026: 23 Unity Industry resources, from an F1 Academy simulator to five Industry Summit sessions.
body_markdown:
## **What did you miss at Industry Summit and Unite Seoul?**


Unity’s customers took to the stages and shared their experiences of Unity’s real-time 3D tools.


### [How Lufthansa Cargo is training aircraft loading supervisors in VR with Unity](https://unity.com/resources/nmy-lufthansa-cargo-xr-training)


Supervisor training normally needs a live flight, an expensive simulator, or both. NMY and Lufthansa Cargo built RampVR to remove that dependency. Trainees walk around a freighter and find randomly generated mistakes on cargo containers and pallets, while trainers run several sessions remotely. Lufthansa Aviation Training reports a 75% reduction in training costs, and Lufthansa Cargo estimates up to 50% fewer operational faults.


### [TomTom and Unity: How AI, maps and real-time 3D take us beyond navigation](https://unity.com/resources/tomtom-real-time-3d-in-car-navigation)


Paul Hesen, VP of Product at TomTom, argues that drivers experience what they see and trust, not the algorithms behind it. In a TomTom simulator study built in Unity, lane-level guidance reduced navigation errors by about 40%. They discovered that 3D detail matters most at start-up, on arrival, and at complex junctions. But on the move, the road comes first.


### [All day in the cab: How Unicontrol built a Unity HMI that operators actually like](https://unity.com/resources/unicontrol-machine-control-hmi)


Mark Povlsen, Software Manager at Unicontrol, explains why a machine control app should feel like a game. Live 3D and color-coded bars replace numbers: green is on target, yellow is approaching, red means too deep. The Android-native app runs on a range of tablets, so distributors can match hardware to what is suitable for each market.


### [How PALFINGER put real-time crane simulation in the browser with Unity](https://unity.com/resources/palfinger-palshow-crane-simulation)


PALFINGER built PALSHOW with Unity WebGL so sales teams get a lifting-capacity answer in a couple of clicks. The team moved it out of a heavy desktop application and reused its calculation framework in the browser. PALSHOW now has 600+ active users a month, and releases rose from two or three a year to more than 12.


### [How CEA rehearses fusion reactor operations in Unity before building a mockup](https://unity.com/resources/cea-fusion-engineering-simulation)


Stéphane Gazzotti, who leads the VIPER platform at CEA’s fusion institute, shows 15 years of simulation work for the WEST and ITER tokamaks (experimental fusion reactors used to study nuclear fusion). One ITER room holds 30 million polygons, and the overall data runs to 20 terabytes. The application runs through procedures of about 500 steps, including operators in ventilated suits who cannot hear. The team uses it to cut radiation exposure by removing unnecessary steps, and builds one physical mockup instead of several.


### [Tata Daewoo: validating vehicle noise, vibration and harshness in virtual reality](https://unity.com/resources/tata-daewoo-virtual-nvh-validation)


Jinyoung Park, an NVH (noise, vibration, and harshness) engineer at Tata Daewoo Mobility, built a standalone VR tool that lets anyone hear and inspect a truck’s noise sources at full scale. Trucks come in many variants, so prototyping each one is not an option. Park used[Unity Asset Transformer](https://unity.com/products/unity-asset-transformer) to cut one CAD model from 29 million triangles to about 2.7 million so it runs on a headset. He reports about 95% accuracy on the NVH spectrum.


### [KITECH: Building a factory digital twin and synthetic data pipeline for manufacturing AI](https://unity.com/resources/kitech-synthetic-data-pipeline-manufacturing-ai)


Dr. Hong-In Won of the Korea Institute of Industrial Technology and Woojin Park of Unity Korea walk through a 14-week, two-part project. First, a foundry digital twin built from point cloud data, with no CAD. Second, a synthetic data pipeline for human-robot collaboration, where bounding boxes and segmentation labels come from the simulation state instead of manual annotation. The dataset has 17 episodes and more than 100,000 raw frames, synchronized at 20 Hz.
